p: The zoo's new home on the northern edge of Bristol means it's a doddle to reach from the motorway, and you're in a part of the city with some brilliant extras close by.

Aerospace Bristol at Filton is just a few minutes down the road and is home to Concorde Alpha Foxtrot, the last Concorde ever to fly. Bristol has a long history of building aircraft, and the museum tells that story with planes, engines and hands-on displays. It's an easy second stop for older kids and any grown-up who remembers that famous sonic boom. The Mall at Cribbs Causeway is also right next to the zoo if you need lunch, a rainy-hour fallback or a bit of shopping on the way home.

For greenery, Blaise Castle Estate in Henbury has woodland walks, a big play area and a little folly castle on the hill, and entry to the grounds is free. Then there's the classic Bristol combo of Clifton and the harbourside further into the city: the Clifton Suspension Bridge across the Avon Gorge, Brunel's SS Great Britain and the We The Curious science centre all make cracking days out in their own right.

For the zoo itself, give it most of a day. The site is spread out and the animals have plenty of room, which means you'll do more walking and waiting than at an old-style zoo. Patience pays off: the bears and big cats often wander into view if you give them a few minutes.
